issues.legal_issue: A reviewing tribunal may not reappreciate evidence and substitute its own finding for a disciplinary authority’s finding when that finding is supported by evidence on the record.
material_facts: A public employee faced a disciplinary charge of demanding and receiving illegal gratification in connection with mutation of land records.
A disciplinary enquiry was conducted, the employee had an opportunity to defend himself, and the disciplinary authority found the charge proved and removed him from service.
The tribunal reassessed the complainant’s evidence, considered it discrepant, and concluded that the charge had not been proved.
The Supreme Court found that the tribunal had substituted its own assessment of the evidence despite the disciplinary finding being based on evidence.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal committed an error of law by reappreciating the evidence and substituting its own finding. Its order was set aside, the transferred application was dismissed, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial review of disciplinary action is review of the manner in which the decision was made, not an appeal on the merits. The disciplinary authority has exclusive responsibility for assessing the evidence and deciding whether a charge is proved. A reviewing court or tribunal may examine whether the finding is supported by evidence or is based on no evidence, but may not reappreciate evidence and reach its own conclusion when the finding is supported by evidence. The Court applied the principles in B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India, State of Tamil Nadu v. T.V. Venugopalan, Union of India v. Upendra Singh, Government of Tamil Nadu v. A. Rajapandian, and Union of India v. B.S. Chaturvedi, in the context of Articles 226 and 323A of the Constitution and the Central Administrative Tribunal Act.

predicates.disciplinary_service_review: A reviewing body considered a challenge to disciplinary action concerning a public employee’s service.
predicates.authority_finding_supported_by_evidence: The disciplinary authority’s finding that the charge was proved rested on evidence in the record.
predicates.reviewing_body_reassessed_evidence: The reviewing body reassessed the evidence and substituted its own conclusion on whether the charge was proved.
predicates.reviewing_body_exceeded_judicial_review: The reviewing body went beyond judicial review by substituting its own finding for an evidence-supported disciplinary finding.

issues.definition: When a reviewing body considers disciplinary action in a public employee’s service, the disciplinary finding is supported by evidence, and the reviewing body reassesses that evidence, the reviewing body exceeds judicial review by substituting its own finding.
